clue.text: Jilted lover writes online story for financial benefit

parts.note: a former partner is an ex
to pen is to write, so writes gives pens
E is the prefix for electronic or online, as in e-commerce
an account is a narrative or story

explanation.surface: A spurned partner turns the break-up into a web serial and makes money from it.
explanation.definitionFit: An expense account is a perk letting an employee charge costs to the firm, a financial benefit of the job.

clue.text: Leave camp's position with terribly imprecise scout

indicators.note: terribly suggests the words are badly done, so the letters of imprecise scout are rearranged

explanation.surface: A careless boy scout is sent to report on where the troop's camp is pitched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave camp' looks like an outdoor scene but is the Brexit campaign to leave the EU; its position is hostility to Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Euroscepticism, distrust of the European Union, was the stance of those campaigning for Britain to leave it.

clue.text: Tending to follow Putin's lead, possibly bent

indicators.note: the word for tending comes after the letter from Putin, so it follows it
the lead of a word is its first letter, here of Putin's

parts.note: liable means tending or inclined to do something

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to toe the Kremlin line may well be corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' in the surface means crooked; in the definition it means flexed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pliable is flexible, so it can be bent, which is what possibly bent describes.

clue.text: Little work requiring 15 days and lots of character?

parts.note: fifteen days is half of November, so take the first half of that month's name

indicators.note: lots of a word is most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: A short piece of writing that takes a fortnight and is full of personalities.
explanation.walkthrough: The 15 is not a cross-reference: half of November's thirty days gives the first half of its name. 'Lots of' cuts the last letter from LETTER, giving LETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel, a little literary work.

clue.text: Part of city street crossed by European on main track

indicators.note: in a down clue the European sits on top of the record term
the street is crossed by the other pieces, sitting inside them

parts.note: the A-side is the main track of a single record

explanation.surface: A European walks a street that crosses a main railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main track' sounds like a railway line; it is the A-side of a pop single.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Side is a district of a city, famously Manhattan's.

clue.text: Station guards left large building

indicators.note: the social rank surrounds the letter as a guard surrounds a prisoner

parts.note: station in the sense of social rank is caste

explanation.surface: Railway station staff protect a large building nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' is social standing, not a railway stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a big fortified residence, a large building.

clue.text: Something in perfume has men and gentleman spinning

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

indicators.note: spinning turns the word for a gentleman round so it reads backwards

parts.note: sir is the title or address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A cologne makes soldiers and a toff go dizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris root, from the iris, is a fixative used in perfumery, so it is an ingredient of scent.

clue.text: Turning in century, man in game's making a score

indicators.note: turning reverses the little word in

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
the king is a piece, or man, in chess

explanation.surface: A batsman on a hundred turns the game and runs up a big total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests runs, but here it is a notch or scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick something is to cut a notch or scratch in it, so nicking is making a score.

clue.text: Lenin, with sigh, resolved to tour steppe, unpretentiously

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round, or tour, the word for steppe
resolved means broken down and reformed, so the letters of Lenin and sigh are rearranged

parts.note: a steppe is a vast grassy plain

explanation.surface: Lenin sighs and decides to travel the Russian grasslands, without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' looks like Lenin's decision but signals the anagram (giving INENGLISH); 'to tour' places the grassland word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something simply, without jargon or show, is saying it in clear plain terms, unpretentiously.

clue.text: Seeks further profit from check clothing

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain, so rein means check
vests are items of clothing

explanation.surface: An investor looks for more gains from a check-patterned garment line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like a pattern on the clothing; it is a verb meaning restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinvest is to put returns back into an investment, seeking further profit.

clue.text: Lag behind army corps, gathering information for the Americans

indicators.note: the convict comes behind, after, the army corps

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a lag is a convict, a con

explanation.surface: An army unit falls behind while doing reconnaissance for US forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lag' looks like a verb meaning trail; it is the noun for an old convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Recon is American shorthand for reconnaissance, the gathering of military intelligence.

clue.text: Scales part of extremely stony, black, bare hill

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, taking the first and last letters of stony

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: a bare word is stripped of its outer letters, leaving the middle of hill

explanation.surface: A climber scales a stony, dark, treeless hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scales' is not climbing but the actress Prunella Scales, who played Sybil Fawlty in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunella Scales's best-known role was Basil Fawlty's wife in Fawlty Towers, so it is the actress's part.

clue.text: Assistant wrapping small hands round beer and oversexed American?

indicators.note: the small letter and the hands wrap around the other pieces
the outer pieces go round the beer and the American, holding them inside

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left, a pair of hands
ales are beers
the wartime British jibe called GIs overpaid, oversexed and over here

explanation.surface: A shop worker gift-wraps a beer for a lecherous US serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oversexed' recalls the British wartime complaint about American soldiers: 'overpaid, oversexed and over here'.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesgirl is a shop assistant, a young woman serving customers.

clue.text: Fair game to pocket diamonds, around 7 or 8?

parts.note: even means fair or balanced

indicators.note: the match takes the diamonds into it as into a pocket

parts.note: a tie is a match or game, as in a cup tie
D is the card-playing abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A fairground game player pockets diamonds at about seven or eight o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair game' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces; a cup tie is a knockout match in British football.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the time around seven or eight o'clock.

clue.text: Cut clothing for girl, one wild child

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass

indicators.note: the clothing of a word is its outer letters, here of girl

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Clothes are cut down for a girl, one of them an unruly child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing for' looks like dress; it takes the outside letters of girl, G and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Mowgli is the feral boy raised by wolves in Kipling's The Jungle Book, a literal child of the wild.

clue.text: Doctor's promise to squeeze writer's back

indicators.note: the vow squeezes the reversed writers between its letters

parts.note: an oath is a solemn promise

indicators.note: back means the word for writers is read backwards

parts.note: the possessive of poet sounds and spells like poets, writers of verse

explanation.surface: A doctor's pledge is to squeeze an author's back.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath is a practitioner who treats the bones and muscles by manipulation, a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Lady's boring design, flipping tasteless white stuff

indicators.note: the woman bores into, sitting inside, the reversed word for design
flipping turns the word for design so it reads backwards

parts.note: aim means design or intention
Agnes is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman's dull pattern, cursed as flipping dreary white stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' and 'flipping' read as mild curses about the design; they are the container and reversal signals, the reversal making MIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesia, magnesium oxide, is a white tasteless powder used as an antacid.

clue.text: Haulier short of right fare down under

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the letter for right is removed

parts.note: a haulier who drives a lorry is a trucker

explanation.surface: A lorry driver lacks the right money for his trip across Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a ticket price; it is food.
explanation.definitionFit: Tucker is Australian slang for food, the fare eaten down under.

clue.text: It's fabulous being rich, a poor compiler's gathered

indicators.note: the compiler is gathered in, inside the rearranged letters
poor indicates the letters of rich and a are badly arranged

parts.note: the crossword compiler refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: It is wonderful being wealthy, an underpaid setter has concluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathered' seems to mean concluded but is the container signal; 'poor' gives the anagram CHIRA, which the setter splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a monster of Greek myth, part lion, goat and serpent, so a creature of fable.

clue.text: This pace is wrong for take-off

indicators.note: wrong signals the letters of this pace are set out incorrectly

explanation.surface: A pilot complains the runway speed is wrong for getting airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take-off' suggests flight; it means a parody.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is an imitation of another work's style, a take-off or send-up.

clue.text: Target for red vehicle skirting unknown, hot area

indicators.note: the vehicle goes round, skirting, the unknown

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
Z is an algebraic unknown
in means fashionable, hot

explanation.surface: A car aimed at a red light dodges an unknown hot zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' means a Bolshevik; the Russian empress was a target for the revolutionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The last Tsarina, Alexandra, was killed by the Bolsheviks, so she was a target for Reds.

clue.text: Knocks seaman over on junk

indicators.note: in a down clue the reversed sailor sits on the junk
over means turned over, so the word for seaman is read backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
tat is cheap rubbish, junk

explanation.surface: A sailor falls over on a Chinese ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' suggests the Chinese boat; it is trash.
explanation.definitionFit: Rat-tat imitates the sound of repeated knocking on a door.

clue.text: Leader from English paper: wonderful, penetrating feature

indicators.note: the other pieces penetrate, going inside, the facial feature

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
FT is the Financial Times newspaper
A1, written AI, means first-rate or wonderful

explanation.surface: An editorial in an English paper is praised as wonderful and incisive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a newspaper editorial in the scene; it is a clan head.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the head of a clan or tribe, its leader.

clue.text: Scoffed at University Blue

parts.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed implies fed
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Mocked at a university that awarded a sporting blue.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sports honour, the surface's misdirection; here blue means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue and being fed up both mean low, unhappy or depressed.

clue.text: Love getting called a hairy beast

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
called on the phone means rang

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is insulted as a shaggy animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang, short for orang-utan, is a shaggy red-haired ape.

clue.text: Clip top from sargasso weed

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, here of sargasso

parts.note: weed read as the past tense of wee means urinated

explanation.surface: A gardener trims the top off some floating seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' is not a plant here but the past tense of the verb to wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip as a noun means a rate, as in going at a fair clip, so it is a synonym for velocity.

clue.text: Switch contains electrical current conductor

indicators.note: to switch is to change round, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: An electrical switch has current running through a conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' in the electrical scene is a musical conductor; 'contains' is not an indicator but fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a famous Italian orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Green area's politicians admitted to loathing bill by Tory PM

indicators.note: the politicians are let into the word for loathing

parts.note: hate is loathing
MPs are Members of Parliament
an ad is an advertisement or bill
Edward Heath was a Conservative British prime minister

explanation.surface: Politicians admit despising a law proposed by a Conservative prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampstead Heath is a large open park in north London; 'bill' looks like a law but is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampstead Heath is a large open parkland in London, a green space.
